text:
leah.c: Noticed flaky behavior in the Go SDK generator streaming sample during onboarding lab. Ctrl-C or context timeout sometimes leaves the CLI process stuck and pprof shows goroutines stuck in net.Conn.Write.

mike.s: can you share the sample? maybe the loop isn't selecting on ctx.Done.

leah.c: minimal repro we hand out in the quickstart:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 4*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator().Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for {
  ch, err := stream.Recv()
  if err != nil { break }
  fmt.Print(ch.Text)
}
```
If the timeout hits the behavior varies: usually Recv returns context.Canceled or EOF, but ~1/10 runs it prints a trailing word and then the program hangs.

vinod.r: this smells like a race between auth refresh/write and ctx cancellation. Our HTTP token refresher does a small write when renewing. If that write races with cancel it can leave the connection in a state where Recv returns a fragment then blocks.

mike.s: UX suggestion: SDK should provide Clear cancellation primitives and well-documented semantics. Two concrete asks: (1) Stream.CloseWithError(err) so callers can signal an explicit reason; (2) guarantee: Recv never returns a non-nil chunk with a non-nil error.

leah.c: I hacked a workaround in the sample by wrapping Recv with select on ctx.Done and calling stream.Close() in the cancel path. That reduced occurrences but didn't eliminate them. sample:
```go
for {
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
    _ = stream.Close()
    return ctx.Err()
  default:
  }
  ch, err := stream.Recv()
  if err != nil { return err }
  fmt.Print(ch.Text)
}
```
But Close() is best-effort and can race; CloseWithError would be nicer so runtime can return the exact error to Recv.

anya.docs: from an onboarding standpoint this is painful. New users copy the quickstart and hit a hung CLI. Can we add a short troubleshooting box in the quickstart like "If your CLI hangs after cancel, use CloseWithError pattern" and link to a sample. Also add a note about auth refresh: "do not expect automatic retries for streaming endpoints".

vinod.r: runtime plan: implement Stream.CloseWithError(err error) and make it idempotent and safe to call from signal handlers. Ensure Recv semantics: if err != nil then chunk == nil. On auth side disable automatic mid-stream refresh/retry; instead surface a clear 401 error to the client so they can decide to re-open.

mike.s: also small API ergonomics: consider providing a convenience helper in the SDK sample: func DrainedRecv(ctx context.Context, s Stream) (string, error) that handles the select+recv loop, so quickstarts show a recommended safe pattern without boilerplate.

leah.c: +1 for helper. Will make a tiny example for the CLI quickstart and pin it until API lands. I'll open a PR with example + integration test that runs with -race and validates no goroutine leaks under pprof.

ci-bot: CI: integration/stream-cancelation-test started by leah.c (go-integration, race)

vinod.r: one more note: docs should explain partial output semantics. If a stream errors after emitting tokens, that output is partial and shouldn't be treated as complete; recommend storing intermediate checkpoints or idempotent consumption patterns.

anya.docs: I'll draft a one-paragraph "why generators sometimes produce partial output" and link to the helper sample. Also add a troubleshooting FAQ entry in the Console docs for "generator kept running after Ctrl-C".

mike.s: for runtime checks: add unit tests that simulate mid-stream 401 and verify the client receives a clear error and no duplicate tail fragments are emitted.

leah.c: thanks folks. I'll push the quickstart PR and reference runtime#623 (WIP) once I have a link. For now I'm updating the onboarding lab to warn about the current behavior. :sparkles:
